literal: He who once showed love will not bestow grace, thinking thus and yearning, behind him who departed you go, foolish my heart!
translation: O my foolish heart! Yearning and thinking, 'He who once showed love will no longer bestow his grace,' you still go running after him who departed.
modern: முன்பு அன்பு காட்டியவர் இப்போது அருள் செய்யமாட்டார் என்று ஏங்கி வருந்தியும், நம்மை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்றவரின் பின்னே போகிறாய்; என் நெஞ்சமே, நீ மிகவும் பேதை!
explanation: The heroine addresses her own heart, which is longing to go after her departed lover. She calls her heart foolish ('பேதை') because it is caught in a painful contradiction. On one hand, the heart laments and realizes that the lover, who once showed great affection ('பரிந்தவர்'), has now departed and will not return to bestow his grace ('நல்கார்'). On the other hand, despite knowing this painful truth, the heart still desperately wants to follow him ('பின்செல்வாய்'). This internal dialogue highlights the helplessness of love, where the mind's rational understanding of abandonment is overpowered by the heart's uncontrollable yearning.
